lines: If a pond has a single lily pad that doubles every day and it takes 30 days to cover the whole pond, on what day is the pond half covered?
It's half covered on day 29.
One of the most important, but least intuitive concepts to the human brain is compounding, because compounding looks like almost nothing for a long time until everything happens all at once.
If you're watching this, I bet you're closer to day 29 than you think.
And all you need to do is have the consistency to see day 30.
I love tracking my habits, so I wanted to make an app that shows the exponential curve in real time when you log an activity.
To let cursors agents go to work using their new composer model, and it did not disappoint.
This is what I built when I was away from my computer.
Took me like 10 minutes.

lines: One million dollars on the line, if your friend was tapping the rhythm of happy birthday, could you guess correctly that it was happy birthday?
Seems like a pretty obvious yes, right?
This was actually a Stanford study in 1990, and only 2.5% of people got it right.
The people tapping could hear the melody in their head, and it seemed so obvious, but the listeners just heard random taps.
This is known as the Curse of Knowledge, and it explains why experts make such bad teachers, because they skip steps that seem obvious to them, but aren't obvious to anyone else.
And they're simply unable to see the topic from the perspective of the beginner, which is why beginners have such a huge advantage that nobody talks about.

They have a fresh perspective, and the ability to see the broader picture, because it's not the expert in one field that's most creative, but the polymath that's acquired the ability to learn, and can draw from multiple sources of inspiration.

lines: A few days ago a legendary entrepreneur said we don't go to the comic book store but if the comics were in the newspaper we'd read them.
This quote genuinely shifted my perspective on how the next generation of millionaires is being made.
Because hear me out, Garfield was free in every newspaper, which is how millions came to recognize it.
They made their billions from selling t-shirts and mugs.
Like the genius Gen Z entrepreneurs are not building comic book stores, they are simply appearing in the newspaper.
The single greatest advantage is existing where all the attention lives, which is social media.
And then building a brand to leverage it, because the thing is nobody goes out of their way for a comic book store, but they won't skip it if it's in their hands.

lines: Carl Jung said the people who feel lost are closest to becoming unstoppable.
See, the hardest realization from working at corporate job was that the person I'd spent years trying to become no longer felt like me.
And it scared me because it meant that I was a failure.
I had this idea that if you don't get it right the first time, you're just automatically behind.
And it's because we live in a culture obsessed with certainty.
We idolize people with 10 year plans and polished identities while uncertainty is seen as a weakness.
But in reality, before every single meaningful transformation comes a period of feeling lost and frustrated.
Most people just assume growth feels good, but it doesn't.
It feels like a loss of control over your identity.
But it's where any meaningful change is found.
It allowed me to pursue my dream life and embracing it was the best thing I ever did.
